knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 2.5.2
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement correctly uses simulation to investigate the Normal approximation for sample means?
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: The object to compare is the repeated-sampling distribution of X̄, and changing n reveals convergence behaviour.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Simulate many samples, collect means, and compare their distribution with Normal across n.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Simulating single observations or asserting the theorem without performing the comparison.

choices.label: Repeatedly simulate samples of a fixed size from the parent distribution, record each sample mean, and compare the empirical distribution of means with the relevant Normal approximation across sample sizes.
Simulate one observation from the parent and compare it with a Normal density; this directly tests the CLT for sample means.
State the CLT without simulating repeated samples, because a theorem statement is the same as an empirical comparison.
A skewed parent distribution prevents sample means from ever becoming approximately Normal.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 2.5.2
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Samples come from an Exponential distribution with mean 1. What should repeated simulations show for X̄ at n=5 versus n=100?
knowledge_checks.body: Compare simulated sampling distributions by sample size.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: The CLT approximation improves as n grows, while the mean stays near 1 and its standard deviation shrinks as 1/√n.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: n=5 may remain skewed; n=100 is closer to N(1,0.1²).
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Assuming sample means retain the parent shape or that any sample size gives exact Normality.

choices.label: At n=5 the distribution of X̄ can remain noticeably right-skewed. At n=100 it should be much closer to Normal, centred near 1 with standard deviation about 1/√100=0.1.
Both distributions of X̄ must be exactly Exponential with mean 1 because averaging preserves the parent family.
At n=100 the means remain as skewed as individual Exponential observations because a skewed parent can never yield approximately Normal means.
At n=5 the means are exactly Normal by the CLT, while at n=100 they return to an Exponential shape.
